At Folkestone, we were deposited at a railway station close upon a shingly beach, on which the sea broke in foam, and which J----- reported as strewn with shells and star-fish; behind was the town, with an old church in the midst; and, close, at hand, the pier, where lay the steamer in which we were to embark.

arxiv-2109-13741.title: A functional central limit theorem for the empirical Ripley’s K K -function
arxiv-2109-13741.creator: Christophe Ange Napoléon Biscio, Anne Marie Svane
arxiv-2109-13741.description: Abstract We establish a functional central limit theorem for Ripley’s K K -function for two classes of point processes. One is the class of point processes having exponential decay of correlations and further satisfying a conditional m-dependence condition. The other is a family of Gibbs point processes. We illustrate the use of our theorem for goodness-of-fit tests in simulations.

arxiv-2208-06271.title: The effect of ambient air pollution on birth outcomes in Norway
arxiv-2208-06271.creator: Xiaoguang Ling
arxiv-2208-06271.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xiaoguang Ling. Ambient air pollution is harmful to the fetus even in countries with relatively low levels of pollution. In this paper, I examine the effects of ambient air pollution on birth outcomes in Norway.

arxiv-2212-04904.title: Representations of loop extended Witt algebras
arxiv-2212-04904.creator: Sachin S. Sharma, Priyanshu Chakraborty, Ritesh Kumar Pandey, and S. Eswara Rao
arxiv-2212-04904.description: Abstract . In this paper, we classify irreducible modules for loop extended Witt algebras with finite dimensional weight spaces. They turn out to be either modules with uniformly bounded weight spaces or highest weight modules. We further prove that all these modules are single point evaluation modules ( n ≥ 2 n\geq 2 ).

arxiv-2406-01865.title: The influence of active agent motility on SIRS epidemiological dynamics
arxiv-2406-01865.creator: R. Kailasham, Aditya S. Khair
arxiv-2406-01865.description: Abstract Active Brownian disks moving in two dimensions that exchange information about their internal state stochastically are chosen to model epidemic spread in a self-propelled population of agents under the susceptible-infected-recovered-susceptible (SIRS) framework. The state of infection of an agent, or disk, governs its self-propulsion speed; consequently, the activity of the agents in the system varies in time.

arxiv-2412-06258.title: Enhanced Multi-Object Tracking Using Pose-based Virtual Markers in 3x3 Basketball
arxiv-2412-06258.creator: Li Yin, Calvin Yeung, Qingrui Hu, Jun Ichikawa, Hirotsugu Azechi, Susumu Takahashi, Keisuke Fujii
arxiv-2412-06258.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Li Yin, Calvin Yeung, Qingrui Hu, Jun Ichikawa, Hirotsugu Azechi, Susumu Takahashi, Keisuke Fujii. Multi-object tracking (MOT) is crucial for various multi-agent analyses such as evaluating team sports tactics and player movements and performance. While pedestrian tracking has advanced with Tracking-by-Detection MOT, team sports like basketball pose unique challenges. These challenges include players’ unpredictable movements, frequent close interactions, and visual similarities that complicate pose labeling and lead to significant occlusions, frequent ID switches, and high manual annotation costs.

arxiv-2504-04322.creator: Pei Xu, Yulei Sui, Mark Staples
arxiv-2504-04322.description: Abstract . Debugging and auditing zero-knowledge-compatible smart contracts remains a significant challenge due to the lack of source mapping in compilers such as zkSolc . In this work, we present a preliminary source mapping framework that establishes traceability between Solidity source code, LLVM IR, and zkEVM bytecode within the zkSolc compilation pipeline.

arxiv-2511-12510.title: Do nineteenth-century graphics still work for today’s readers?
arxiv-2511-12510.creator: Yingke He
arxiv-2511-12510.description: Abstract Do nineteenth-century graphics still work for today’s readers? To investigate this question, we conducted a controlled experiment evaluating three canonical historical visualizations—Nightingale’s polar area diagram, Playfair’s trade balance chart, and Minard’s campaign map—against modern redesigns. Fifty-four participants completed structured question-answering tasks, allowing us to measure accuracy, response time, and perceived workload (NASA–TLX).

pmc-10632445.title: Detection of Wuchereria bancrofti in human blood samples and mosquitoes in Matayos, Busia County-Kenya
pmc-10632445.creator: Nancy Kinyatta, Dorcas Wachira, Rosemary Githae, Japheth Lusweti, Johnstone Ingonga, Christine Ichugu, Caroline Maina, Rukiya Haji, Francis Kimani, Rael Musili, Jacinta Muli, Luna Kamau
pmc-10632445.description: Lymphatic filariasis is a mosquito borne disease which leads to abnormal painful enlarged body parts, severe disability and social stigma. We screened Wuchereria bancrofti in Matayos constituency in Busia County. Blood samples were collected from 23 villages selected purposively based on clinical case reports. Finger prick and/or venous blood sampling and mosquito collections was carried out.

pmc-11437188.title: Agile perching maneuvers in birds and morphing-wing drones
pmc-11437188.creator: Valentin Wüest, Simon Jeger, Mir Feroskhan, Enrico Ajanic, Fabio Bergonti, Dario Floreano
pmc-11437188.description: Avian perching maneuvers are one of the most frequent and agile flight scenarios, where highly optimized flight trajectories, produced by rapid wing and tail morphing that generate high angular rates and accelerations, reduce kinetic energy at impact. While the behavioral, anatomical, and aerodynamic factors involved in these maneuvers are well described, the underlying control strategies are poorly understood.

pmc-11625439.title: Identification of PANoptosis-Related Genes in Community-Acquired Pneumonia Diagnosis
pmc-11625439.creator: Qiaoxin Hao, Wei Gao, Pei Zhang, Peng Yan
pmc-11625439.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to identify and characterize novel PANoptosis biomarkers for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) diagnosis.MethodsTranscriptomic data from training set GSE196399 and validation sets GSE94916 and GSE202947 were utilized. A PANoptosis gene set was identified by intersecting DEGs linked to CAP, WGCNA hub genes, and PANoptosis-related genes. GO and KEGG analyses were conducted for enrichment analysis.

pmc-12380001.title: Dual EGFR L858R and KRAS G12A Mutations in Lung Adenocarcinoma: A Rare Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-12380001.creator: Gang Wei, Jun Tang, Huaiwen Wang, Dongdong Zhang
pmc-12380001.description: BackgroundKRAS mutations are typically mutually exclusive in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with the G12C mutation being the most common subtype. The coexistence of KRAS and EGFR mutations is exceedingly rare and is typically emerges as a secondary event following acquired resistance to EGFR-targeted therapies.

pmc-12852999.creator: Xi-Lin Yang, Li-Chun Wei, Jian-Li He, Tie-Jun Wang, Li Ran, Li-Juan Zou, Xiao-Ge Sun, Xiao-Mei Li, Zi Liu, Yong-Gang Shi, Sha Li, Feng-Ju Zhao, Kun Gao, Wei Zhong, Guang-Hui Cheng, Ya-Li Gao, Bao-Sheng Sun, Jun-Fang Yan, Fu-Quan Zhang

pmc-13053184.title: Efficacy and Safety of Endourological Surgery for Managing Overactive Bladder Symptoms in Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13053184.creator: Carlo Giulioni, Angelo Cafarelli, Pietro Piazza, Luca Spinozzi, Savio Domenico Pandolfo, Enrico Sicignano, Giacomo Maria Pirola, Simone Scarcella, Valentina Maurizi, Jeremy Yuen-Chun Teoh, Vineet Gauhar, Daniele Castellani
pmc-13053184.description: PurposeTo systematically review the outcomes of endoscopic surgery in men with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) associated with preoperative overactive bladder (OAB) symptoms.MethodsLiterature search was conducted on 12th May 2025 including PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus database. Complication rates were assessed using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel Method with the random effect model and reported as odds ratio, 95% confidence interval (CI), and P-values.

pmc-13196621.creator: Unknown
pmc-13196621.description: 022.2085391 Following publication, internal integrity audits revealed concerns around several authorship changes which were made between submission and acceptance of the article. We have contacted the authors for an explanation, but we have not received a response. As determining authorship and contributions is core to the integrity and accountability of published work, we are therefore retracting the article.

pmc-13317606.title: Early Detection and Inhibition of Post‐Surgical Cancer Recurrence by Synthetic Extracellular Vesicles
pmc-13317606.creator: Junli Zhang, Wenjia Chang, Ruolin Hu, Peiyan Su, Qin Zhou, Yanan Li, Zhenzhong Zhang, Kaixiang Zhang
pmc-13317606.description: Early detection of post‐surgical cancer recurrence could improve patient survival. Endogenous biomarkers remain at the forefront of early detection efforts, but many lack the requisite sensitivity and specificity to effectively guide clinical management. Herein, we employed a synthetic biomarker approach by embedding a tumor specific promoter‐driven synthetic extracellular vesicles (EVs)‐generating system at the tumor resection site.

pmc-13630853.title: AOSNP‐ADAPTR resource level‐based recommendations on practical diagnostic strategies for ependymomas
pmc-13630853.creator: Laveniya Satgunaseelan, Michael E Buckland, Geeta Chacko, Kenta Masui, Junji Shibahara, Vani Santosh, Maysa Al‐Hussaini, Sung‐Hye Park, Tarik Tihan, Ho‐Keung Ng, Pieter Wesseling, David N Louis, Chitra Sarkar, Takashi Komori
pmc-13630853.description: Ependymomas are uncommon primary tumors of the central nervous system (CNS) that affect both children and adults. In recent years, molecular analyses have identified multiple subtypes of ependymal tumors based on location, patterns of CpG island methylation, and gene fusion events.
